h1:
Khao Hin Lek Fai Hua Hin
City and Sea Viewpoint
intro: If you want to see all of Hua Hin in a single frame, Khao Hin Lek Fai is the answer — and you can drive right to the top. At around 162 metres up, you look down over the whole town and the Gulf of Thailand, all the way out to Khao Takiab. There are six viewpoints scattered across the summit, entry is free, and it's open 6am–8pm. Locals come up here to exercise in the early morning and to catch the last light in the evening.

blocks.html: Khao Hin Lek Fai (some people call it Radar Hill because of the radar station on top) sits just west of central Hua Hin, only about 3 kilometres out. The best part is that you don't have to hike — a paved road runs all the way up, and there's a car park for both cars and motorbikes. Once you're up there you can stroll between the various viewpoints at an easy pace, which makes it work for solo travellers, couples, and families with small kids alike.

From the summit you get a wide 180-degree view over Hua Hin. One side looks across the town, the golf course and the beachfront buildings; the other side opens onto the blue Gulf of Thailand, stretching south as far as Khao Takiab. On a clear day the horizon is razor-sharp, and it's the kind of angle where you fit both the town and the sea into one shot.

items: Viewpoints 4 and 5 — these two are the highlight. They're an easy walk and have the most open views, with the town and sea spread out in front of you. This is where people gather to watch the sun come up over the water.
Viewpoint 2 — the spot a lot of people prefer for the last light at sunset, since it faces the mountains to the west.
Viewpoint 6 — looks out over the range behind the town, good for shots with the mountains as a backdrop.
King Rama VII Monument — built by the people of Hua Hin to commemorate his visits to the town. It's on the summit and a place where visitors stop to pay their respects.

blocks.title: Sunrise or sunset?
blocks.html: The sea here is to the east, so the sun rises straight out of the water — that view is clearer and prettier. If you come for sunset, the light drops behind the mountains west of the town, which gives a completely different mood. The sky changes colour beautifully at both times, but if you specifically want the sun lifting clean off the water, come in the pre-dawn hours.

blocks.text: Hours, entry fee, and getting there

items: Opening hours: daily 6am–8pm (the gate closes at 8pm, so head down before then)
Distance: about 3–5 km from central Hua Hin, a 10–15 minute drive
Route: turn in at Hua Hin Soi 70 (Chomsin Road) off Phetkasem Road, then drive straight up the hill to the top. Signs point the way the whole route.
Parking: there's a car park at the summit for both cars and motorbikes

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Parts of the road up are steep and narrow, so if you're in a regular car or on a motorbike, use a low gear and take it slow. On long weekends and Saturdays–Sundays the top car park fills up fast — come early, or arrive about half an hour before sunset, and you'll have an easier time finding a spot. The summit is windy and there aren't many shops, so bring your own water.

blocks.text: A half-day plan around Khao Hin Lek Fai

blocks.html: Khao Hin Lek Fai is close to town, so it's easy to pair with other sights in the same day. Here are two versions depending on whether you're chasing morning or evening light.

items.activity: Leave your hotel and drive up Khao Hin Lek Fai
items.note: Go before dawn so you catch the sun rising out of the sea

items.activity: Head to viewpoints 4–5 for the morning light, shoot the town and sea
items.note: Wear a windbreaker — it's windy in the morning

items.activity: Head back down and find a café or a rice-porridge shop in town for breakfast
Walk the market or visit Hua Hin Railway Station
items.note: Still cool out, so it's pleasant walking

items.activity: Visit Khao Takiab or walk the beach in the late afternoon
items.note: Khao Takiab has lots of monkeys — watch out for them snatching food and anything in your hands

items.activity: Drive up Khao Hin Lek Fai and find parking before sunset
items.note: Parking fills fast on weekends, so leave extra time

items.activity: Settle in at viewpoint 2 for the evening light as the sky changes colour
Head down before dark, then on to a night market or a seafood restaurant for dinner

items.name: Khao Takiab
items.blurb: A small seaside hill south of town with a temple on top and bay views — but loads of monkeys, so keep food and glasses well out of reach.

items.name: Hua Hin Railway Station
items.blurb: A historic Thai-style wooden station with the King Rama VI royal pavilion — a classic photo spot in town.

items.name: Hua Hin Beach
items.blurb: A long sandy beach right in town, good for walking all day — but the wind and surf pick up at times, so check the warning flags before you swim.

faq.q: Is Khao Hin Lek Fai free, and what time does it open?
faq.a: Entry is free with no charge. It's open daily from 6am to 8pm, and the gate closes at 8pm, so head down before closing time.

faq.q: Is sunrise or sunset better at Khao Hin Lek Fai?
faq.a: The sea is to the east, so the sun rises straight out of the water, which is clearer and prettier. If you want the sun lifting clean off the sea, come in the pre-dawn hours and head to viewpoints 4–5. In the evening the light drops behind the mountains — the sky still changes colour beautifully, just with a different mood.

faq.q: Can you drive to the top, or do you have to hike?
faq.a: You can drive all the way to the summit — there's a paved road and a car park for both cars and motorbikes, so no hiking needed. That said, parts of the road are steep and narrow, so drive slowly in a low gear.

faq.q: How far is Khao Hin Lek Fai from central Hua Hin?
faq.a: It's about 3–5 km away, roughly a 10–15 minute drive. Turn in at Hua Hin Soi 70 (Chomsin Road) off Phetkasem Road and drive straight up the hill; there are signs the whole way.

faq.q: Are there any shops or cafés on the hill?
faq.a: Shops on the summit are few and not always open, so bring your own drinking water — especially if you're coming in the pre-dawn hours or near closing. There are plenty of cafés and restaurants down in central Hua Hin, just a few minutes' drive away.
